title: useDebugValue
summary: Add a short label for a custom hook in React DevTools.
nestedConcepts: Add a label to a custom hook
Keep private data out of labels

subtopics.title: Add a label to a custom hook
subtopics.explanation: A custom hook packages reusable stateful behavior behind a function that starts with `use`. `useDebugValue` can add a readable label for that hook while inspecting it in React DevTools. It helps explain what a custom hook represents without adding visible UI.

subtopics.title: Read hook values in DevTools
subtopics.explanation: React DevTools can show the label supplied by `useDebugValue` while inspecting a component’s custom hooks. The label is for development diagnosis; it does not change rendering or send data to users. Use it to clarify a value that would otherwise be difficult to interpret.

subtopics.title: Format expensive labels lazily
subtopics.explanation: When formatting a debug label is expensive, pass a formatting function so React DevTools can request it when needed. A simple value can be passed directly. Avoid calculations on every render when the label is only useful during development inspection.

subtopics.title: Keep private data out of labels
subtopics.explanation: Debug labels can be visible to developers inspecting an application, so do not include passwords, tokens, personal details, or private records. Prefer a safe summary such as a status or item count. Development-only information should still follow the project’s data-handling rules.

subtopics.title: Keep debug labels useful
subtopics.explanation: A short label that names the hook’s current state is easier to scan than a large serialized value. Add `useDebugValue` to custom hooks that are hard to inspect, not to every hook by default. The component’s behavior should remain correct if the label is removed.

foundations.overview: useDebugValue shows a readable label for a custom hook while inspecting a component. It does not change what users see. Use it when a hook hides meaningful state that would otherwise be hard to inspect.
foundations.mentalModel: It is like putting a name tag on a box in a crowded storeroom.
foundations.whyItMatters: Clear labels help developers understand complex state without adding console noise.

keyTakeaways: Custom hooks package reusable stateful behavior.
DevTools can display debug labels for custom hooks.
Format the label only when the extra work is useful.
Do not expose private user information in debug labels.

codeLab.title: Label a custom hook
codeLab.instructions: Create a custom useOnline hook that reads browser online state and gives it a useful DevTools label.
codeLab.expectedOutput: The hook returns a boolean and React DevTools can show an Online or Offline label.
hints: Break the task into state, event handling, and rendered feedback.
Keep the interface accessible with labels and meaningful button text.
